expectations.text: Exactly one Lenis instance is created in the app (no second smooth-scroll library, no autoRaf alongside a manual raf loop)
Lenis is driven by gsap.ticker (gsap.ticker.add calling lenis.raf with time*1000) and gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0) is set
expectations.evidence: gsap.ticker.add(tick) where tick = time => lenis.raf(time*1000); lagSmoothing(0)

expectations.text: ScrollTrigger is updated from Lenis scroll events (lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update) or equivalent)
The CSS rule html { scroll-behavior: smooth } is removed or neutralised because it conflicts with Lenis programmatic scrolling
expectations.evidence: index.css: rule removed; only a comment remains explaining why

expectations.text: In-page anchor navigation scrolls with a 72px (or header-height) offset so sections are not hidden under the fixed header
expectations.evidence: RUNTIME (vite build + Playwright): header nav → #pricing top = 72px; menu link → #faq top = 72px. index.css uses section[id]{scroll-margin-top: var(--header-h)} and the template skips its own offset when CSS margin is present — the iteration-1 double-count is gone

expectations.text: Anchor navigation moves keyboard focus to the target section (e.g. tabindex=-1 + focus) or otherwise preserves accessible focus
expectations.evidence: RUNTIME: activeElement = pricing / faq after clicks

expectations.text: Opening the mobile menu stops scrolling (lenis.stop() or equivalent) and closing it restores scrolling (lenis.start())
expectations.evidence: useScrollLock(open) → lenis.stop/start; RUNTIME wheel blocked while open, scroll works after close

expectations.text: The Lenis instance and the ticker callback are cleaned up on unmount (lenis.destroy() and gsap.ticker.remove)
expectations.evidence: template cleanup: ticker.remove, lagSmoothing restored, destroy()

expectations.text: The Lenis stylesheet (lenis/dist/lenis.css) or equivalent recommended CSS is included
